acceptance: Every develop PR and merge group reports the visual required context; site-changing trees cannot pass when comparison failed, was absent, or lacked a valid exact-base-SHA baseline.
The visual job retains its existing input coverage; any excluded input names the rendered-site dependency it no longer feeds and the accepted coverage loss.
A protected exact-SHA baseline can be produced or recovered after a dropped develop push, without accepting a stale baseline or a PR diagnostic artifact.
The approval path works for intentional visual changes on the exact PR head and does not become an unreviewed merge-group bypass.
The develop-squash-only hosted ruleset requires the new context, and its runbook and drift guard agree with live state; verify a real PR and merge-group result before closeout.
description: Implement the option 3 decision recorded in _project/decisions/public-site-visual-required-check-2026-09-24.md. Preserve the current visual comparison coverage and fail-closed exact-base-SHA semantics. Make an always-reporting required context on every develop pull request and merge group, with an explicit non-applicable success only when the current visual input set is unaffected. Do not directly require the conditional docs.yml visual job. Update the live develop-squash-only ruleset, runbook, and drift guard together. Treat missing exact-SHA baselines as a distinct producer-availability defect within this implementation: add bounded automatic production or recovery of the protected baseline without promoting PR diagnostics, and retain a manual recovery path. Account for exact-head visual approvals and merge-group identity so intentional changes can merge after review.
